subject: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.

messages.author: 3dfa900e3d85281b
messages.subject: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
parts:
I've written already some twenty apps of considerable size, almost all of them in Spanish, but I'm considering to include an English
version. I've discarded a second copy with texts in English, because of expected problems in maintenance of two versions. I'd like
to have a language selector in the same app, and swap the texts dynamically.

However, after some tests with an app, complex enough for finding different kind of difficulties, I give up. Inexplicably at least for me,
the two-language version was making its way until a point where it was behaving unpredictably. Some parts (texts or plots) don't
appear but if I refresh the page in the browser (I'm using a remote server, not Rstudio), it can appear complete, perhaps... Even
worse, sometimes the load finishes with an error message, but after refreshing the page loads partially or maybe totally.

I have to explain that this behaviour has not appeared at some critical point. I was advancing slowly, writing small pieces of code
and checking them carefully before facing another piece. The first times I noticed that the error was not a real error I thought that
the reason could be a mismatch between the remote server and my computer, and the upload was not complete when I tried to
refresh the page (it would be strange anyway, since the files are really small).

As I was advancing in the implementation of the two-language version, obviously the program was increasing in complexity. I wonder
if this can have influence in the app behaviour: I had to convert a number of simple p('blablabla'), HTML('blablabla') and widgets in
renderText and renderUI calls (because of the language dependency), BUT it would be hard to accept that functions like that are
able to degrade the program so much.

So I think that I should return to the starting point, and adopt a different paradigm. I've sought a bit about the topic, but it seems
that translations are not very common, or they don't pose any problem normally. In my case, my initial strategy is:
  • a global environment (.E), with a variable to store the selected language (d): each language has an actionButton, and an observer to update the variable (.E$d)
  • a global list of character arrays; each array with the expression in English and in Spanish
  • Examples of use:
    •   output$titulo = renderText( { .L$titulo[.E$d] } )
    •   output$par2 = renderUI( { HTML(.L$par2[.E$d]) } )
    •   output$Type = renderUI({    radioButtons("tipo", .L$pastel[.E$d], c(.L$pie1[.E$d], .L$pie2[.E$d]), inline=TRUE)  })
Perhaps a clue: I'm using withMathJax too. Is it so toxic that it could be related to that undesirable performance?

Have you any similar experience? Can you propose any other strategy? I will appreciate it so much.

JA

messages.author: 4753f061948056b3
messages.subject: Re: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
parts:
Hi José,

I also tried and tried to implement multi linguality in my shiny apps, and i finaly succeed, with, for me, absolutly no loss of performance.

My solution can be tested in an app dedicated to pigeon racing in Belgium. Languages used are English, French (default), and Duch.
You can test it here : http://www.yapluka.be/sapps/beprmap/
Code available here : https://github.com/gvincke/beprmap

My strategy is :
The language will be selected with a select list (takes less place than radio buttons, and is language number independant when wpeeking about layout).
All translated string are in tab separated CSV files, with a column for the id of the string, and as many column as language (fr, en, nl in my example).
These CSV files are imported in server.R in a dataset, and a function (tr for translate) select the right sentence regarding its ID and the current language.
In the github repos you will find this at lines 61 to 64.
So in my app, server.R side, whe i need a translated sentence, i call it with tr("ID").
It works fine, but...
It means that all inputs fields that would have been defined in ui.R are set ups in server.R and called in ui.R with uiOutput()
If you have select list, you will need to charges them regarding the current language, so each multivalue field will need to have its own CSV tanslated file, and setup the field in ui.R (it must exist before sever.R is excuted) but with empty values, and you fill it from server.R with updateSelectInput() function, after having selected all values from the good CSV file. Exemple at line 51 in ui.R and lines 66-78 in server.R.
At my own experience, it's hard to use this with global navigation like navbarPages(), because the language select list can not be set up for all app independently to some panels, so you must set language in only one page, but the field will not be available in others.
In my exemple, the select input is available in the first tab, but not in the other (Credits). So if you are in Credits tab page, and you want to change language, you have to open first tab page, change language, and re-open the Credits page.

I don't know if my exemple helps you, but it works fine for me.

Regards ,

Grégoire

messages.subject: Re: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
parts: I don't have time at the moment to try to digest Grégoire solution, but I wanted to respond to José's approach:
• a global environment (.E), with a variable to store the selected language (d): each language has an actionButton, and an observer to update the variable (.E$d)

This is NOT correct. Instead of an environment you should use reactiveValues(d = defaultLanguage) (where defaultLanguage whatever you decide), and it should not be global, it MUST be located inside the shinyServer function so that it only applies to that session.
• a global list of character arrays; each array with the expression in English and in Spanish

That's fine--this can be global. Or better than character arrays, how about a data frame that's read from a .csv? Each row is a string, each column is a language. Then you could use a spreadsheet program to edit the string table (remember to both save and read as UTF-8).

• Examples of use:
  •   output$titulo = renderText( { .L$titulo[.E$d] } )
  •   output$par2 = renderUI( { HTML(.L$par2[.E$d]) } )
  •   output$Type = renderUI({    radioButtons("tipo", .L$pastel[.E$d], c(.L$pie1[.E$d], .L$pie2[.E$d]), inline=TRUE)  })

Better to create a wrapper function within the shinyServer function that does this for you, as I believe Grégoire is suggesting.

tr <- function(stringId) {
  .L[[stringId]][.E$d]
}

parts:
Hi Grégoire and Joe.
Thank you very much for your contributions. I'll take advantage of them. 
I've isolated a bit the root of the problem. Unfortunately, I was not able to go further.
It's something related with withMathJax when it's on the server side. If the call is made
from the ui side, everything works well. Obviously, it's not a matter on performance, as
I pointed out the first time.

The ui code is something like: uiOutput("test")   (among some other similar functions)

On the other side: 
  output$test = renderUI({
    withMathJax( p('\\(= \\sum_j \\sum_i (y_{i,j} - \\bar{Y})^2 \\)'))
  } )

Notice that this is simpler tan real: no translations here, though this doesn't make a difference, I guess.
Actually, the page loads this with no problems: the headache is related with its interferences with
other blocks, which don't appear, or appear after refreshing the page, or not appear at all.

I'm aware that I'm not including relevant information here. I would ask for help to anyone which
experienced problems with MathJax once, or they know about documentation on mathJax + Shiny.
Or simply stay tuned until I made some progress.

Well, merci bien tous les deux

JA

messages.subject: Re: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
parts:
Hi everybody,

I'd like to finish this thread with my conclusions. First of all, I can't see nothing that relates performance with the use of render**
to translate the texts. But there is something irregular with MathJax: if you need to use it for strings containing latex code, you
have to put withMathJax() once in ui.R, and likely again inside the render**() function. Otherwise, you will obtain strange results.

With regard to the original subject of my question, I managed to sort it out like this:
  • the texts are written in a UTF-8 ascii file, with three columns separated by tabs: label, sentence in English, sentence in Spanish. Don't write double backslash (\\) for latex since R will double each one. I haven't used excel to write the texts, the csv, tab-separated version included quotes ("), arbitrarily put by excel! (well, probably excel did it for some reason, but I couldn't guess it)
  • server.R includes the line. .L = read.table(<<file with texts>>, header=FALSE, sep='\t', quote="", row.names=1, colClasses=rep("character", 3))
  • it also includes the code 
  .E <- reactiveValues(d = 1)  #active language and default
  tr <- function(stringId) {
        .L[stringId, .E$d]
  }
        • ui.R begins with: Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "es_ES.UTF-8") #to be sure that accents in text will be allowed in plots, thanks Grégoire
        • Put two flags in the top right corner with (the images have to be in the www folder):
          absolutePanel(
            top = 0, right = 0, width=80, fluidRow(actionButton("eng", img(src='uk-icon.png'), style="margin:0;padding:0;"),
                                                   actionButton("spa", img(src='Spain-icon.png'), style="margin:0;padding:0;"))
          ),
                • Write two observers in server.R to update the active language:
                  observeEvent(input$eng, {    .E$d=1   })
                  observeEvent(input$spa, {    .E$d=2   })
                  • Replace the literal strings by calls to textOutput or uiOutput, with their correspondent render** in server.R. Example:
                    • uiOutput("parrafo"),
                    • output$parrafo = renderText( { tr("parrafo") } )
                  Hope it helps to others. Regards,
